title: CI: daily super run failed
thread:
**Issue #3078 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3078: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41916338238](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41916338238) on `main` (`4e0b3b0`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e (7/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41916338238/job/126881724978) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `main`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`): production promotes itself only from a run on `main` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41922080444)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Root cause is inferred, not confirmed.** I could not open the job log (no GitHub access, and no Cypress, `node_modules` or network in the planning sandbox). The plan below is built from reading the code, and the builder must say so in the PR.

## Goal

Make the daily super run's `e2e (7/8)` job pass. The task asks for a root-caused fix, a robust test (not a skip or exception), and a PR that names the job it fixes and how it was checked.

Shard 7 plays specs 10, 13, 15, 17, 25, 31, 38 and 48. Specs 10 and 13 run on every PR (the smoke list), so they are unlikely to have broken.

The most probable cause is spec 38's axe check of `/patch-notes` at 1280x720. Patch #3036 (after the #3021 axe fix) added the patch-notes legend. `.patch-legend__micros-toggle` in `apps/web/src/patches/patches.css` has no minimum height on desktop:
- It is 13px text at line-height 1.35 plus 2px padding top and bottom, about 21.6 px tall.
- It sits directly under `.patch-legend__link`.
- That fails axe `target-size` (WCAG 2.5.8, serious), the same rule class #3021 handled for the phone piles.
- Only the `@media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 600px)` block makes it 44 px. That is why phone and spec 47 (smoke, phone) pass.

The real `patches.json` has many micro patches (`v0.5.11b`…`o`), so the toggles exist on the live page.

There is also a flake. `PatchNotes` shows the route's screen at once and a skeleton until `source.patches()` resolves, and the legend exists only after that. Spec 38 waits only for `patchTestid.screen`, so axe sometimes checks the skeleton and passes. Spec 38 must wait for the legend so it checks the loaded page every time.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/patches/patches.css` | change | Add `min-height: 32px` to the shared rule for `.patch-legend__micros-toggle` / `.patch-legend__toggle` ("A patch's micros: a small control…"). |
| `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx` | change | New `it("R3012000 …")` guard test reading `patches.css`. |
| `e2e/cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts` | change | The `/patch-notes` test waits for `patchTestid.legend` before axe. |
| `spec/rulings/R3012000.md` | change | One sentence on the desktop 24 px floor (spec first, CLAUDE.md rule 1). |

The builder must not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`.
- `e2e/support/axe-exceptions.ts`. No new exception; "Never" rule 2 forbids weakening the check.
- Any crate under `crates/`.

Governing text: R3012000 (the legend), R2122000 (44 px on touch), SPEC §10.10, issue #757 (spec 38, WCAG 2.2 AA). No new ruling is needed: this is a stylesheet defect against an existing target (WCAG 2.2 AA), not a rules decision. So there is no `spec/pending/` file and no `cargo jackioh spec index`.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/patches/patches.css`**
   - Find the rule that starts with the comment `/* A patch's micros: a small control under its link that shows or hides them. */`.
   - Its selectors are `.tavern.app-shell .patch-notes .patch-legend__micros-toggle,` and `.tavern.app-shell .patch-notes .patch-legend__toggle {`.
   - After its `align-items: center;` line add:
     ```css
       /* WCAG 2.5.8 (e2e spec 38): 13px text with 2px padding measures about 22px, under the 24px a mouse's target needs
          beside the link above it. The touch block below makes it 44px (R2122000). */
       min-height: 32px;
     ```
   - 32px matches `.patch-name`'s desktop floor, in the same file.
   - Do not move or reorder rules. The later `.patch-legend__toggle { min-height: 44px }` rule and the `@media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 600px)` block have the same specificity and come later, so they still win for the phone drawer button and for touch.

2. **`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`**
   - Add the test below as the last `it` of the outermost `describe`, right after `"R3012000 the stylesheet keeps the phone page from scrolling sideways, and the legend sticky"`. Reuse the file's `readFileSync`, `resolve`, `dirname`, `fileURLToPath`.
     ```ts
     it("R3012000 the legend's micro patches button is at least 24 px tall with a mouse (WCAG 2.5.8, e2e spec 38)", () => {
       const MIN_TARGET_PX = 24;
       const css = readFileSync(resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "patches.css"), "utf8");
       const rule = /\.patch-legend__micros-toggle,\s*\.tavern\.app-shell \.patch-notes \.patch-legend__toggle \{([^}]*)\}/u.exec(css);
       expect(rule).not.toBeNull();
       const height = Number(/min-height:\s*(\d+)px/u.exec(rule?.[1] ?? "")?.[1] ?? 0);
       expect(height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MIN_TARGET_PX);
     });
     ```
   - The title carries `R3012000`, which is already in the note's `proven_in` for this file.

3. **`e2e/cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts`**
   - In `describe("public pages")`, replace the body of `it("/patch-notes", …)`, which is currently `checkPublic(at("/patch-notes"), "/patch-notes", patchTestid.screen);`, with:
     ```ts
     cy.visit("/patch-notes");
     cy.get(ts(patchTestid.screen), { timeout: timeouts.view }).should("be.visible");
     // The screen shows at once; the legend (R3012000) and the entries only once the history has loaded:
     // checked with them on the page, never against the skeleton that comes first.
     cy.get(ts(patchTestid.legend), { timeout: timeouts.view }).should("be.visible");
     expectNoBlockingViolations(at("/patch-notes"));
     ```
   - `patchTestid`, `ts`, `timeouts` and `expectNoBlockingViolations` are already imported there.
   - On a phone the legend `<nav>` is the visible drawer bar, so the wait holds at both widths.

4. **`spec/rulings/R3012000.md`**
   - At the end of the second paragraph, after the sentence ending "…every legend control is a 44 px target on a touch screen or a narrow window ([[R2122000]])", add:
     "With a mouse its controls are at least 24 px tall too (WCAG 2.5.8, e2e spec 38); the micro patches button is 32 px, as a card's name button on this page is."
   - Leave the front matter alone.

5. **Reproduce first if the tooling allows** (the builder may have it; the planner did not)
   - Before step 1, run spec 38 against a built client and a release server, as `.github/actions/e2e-shard/action.yml` does:
     - `E2E=1 pnpm --dir apps/web build:e2e`
     - `cargo build --release -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-tools`
     - start the client and server, then `cd e2e && pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts`
   - Expect `/patch-notes` to fail with `target-size` on `.patch-legend__micros-toggle`, then pass after step 1.
   - If it fails on a different route or rule, fix that real defect instead and say so in the PR.
   - If Cypress cannot run, skip this step and state it in the PR.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`: the new `it("R3012000 the legend's micro patches button is at least 24 px tall …")` fails without step 1 and passes with it.
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/typescale.test.ts src/palette.test.ts` (no font-size or colour was touched)
- `e2e/cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts`: the `/patch-notes` test now always checks the loaded page. It runs daily only (not on PRs). If the tooling exists:
  - `cd e2e && pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts`
  - `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck`
- `cargo jackioh spec check` (a ruling note and a cited R-id changed).

## Done when

- [ ] `.patch-legend__micros-toggle` has a desktop `min-height` of at least 24px (32px), and the touch and narrow block still gives 44px.
- [ ] Spec 38's `/patch-notes` test waits for the legend before axe, at both widths.
- [ ] The new unit test and the rest of `PatchNotes.test.tsx` pass.
- [ ] R3012000's note carries the sentence, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green.
- [ ] No new axe exception, `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`, and nothing under the forbidden paths changed.
- [ ] Checks green: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e`, and `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck` if reachable.
- [ ] PR text names the job (`e2e (7/8)`, spec 38 `/patch-notes`) and says whether spec 38 was run: either that it failed before and passed after, or that it could not be run and the cause is inferred from code. It must not claim the super run is green; only the next daily run shows that.

## Risks

- **The cause may be wrong.** Other shard-7 specs (15, 17, 25, 31, 48) changed nothing in my reading, but nothing proves they pass. If the next run's `e2e (7/8)` is still red, the failing spec and test name from the log are needed (see Open questions).
- **Layout:** each legend micro-patches button grows from about 22px to 32px, and the legend scrolls (`max-height`). Phone and touch keep 44px through the later media block. Do not reorder rules in `patches.css`.
- **Spec 47** (smoke, phone) also checks `/patch-notes` only for `patchTestid.screen`. It is unaffected and left alone.
- **Rule 7 and determinism:** nothing here touches engine, hidden information or `Rng`. This is CSS plus tests only.

## Open questions

- **Needs a person's input:** the planner could not read the job log of run 41916338238. If the next daily run still fails `e2e (7/8)`, someone should paste the failing spec and test name from the job log into the issue.
- No workflow or `.github/` change is needed for this fix.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````
